title: comparing very long numeric prereleases
issue_text:
My service takes version strings from outside sources, screens them with Version.is_valid and sorts whatever passes. On Python 3.11 with semver 3.1.0, a version whose prerelease has an all-digit identifier over 4300 digits long gets through that check, but comparing it then crashes, even against an identical version:

```python
import semver

big = "2.0.0-" + "7" * 5000
semver.Version.is_valid(big)              # True
semver.Version.parse(big).compare(big)    # ValueError: Exceeds the limit for integer string conversion
semver.compare(big, "2.0.0-3")            # same ValueError
```

A major, minor or patch number of that length is rejected by is_valid, and I can live with that.

I expected anything is_valid approves to be sortable. These long prereleases are legal SemVer, so is_valid should keep accepting them and compare should order them numerically. Nothing else should change: comparing any other value, including a Version built directly with prerelease text that parse would reject, must give the same results and errors as today.
